intent.goal: Read WIP-curve evidence only from the report's WIP-curve section, so a complete-looking wave= row quoted in a fenced example, a deviations table or another section can neither bind as the run's evidence nor trip the duplicate/stray/unmeasured-row checks against the real rows, while every per-wave completeness check keeps running on the section's rows.
intent.ruled_out: Requiring the full template heading text (the module's own '## WIP curve' fixtures, used by every pre-existing WIP-curve test, would stop opening the section, and the 2026-08-28 ship-it report's heading differs after 'row'); matching any heading that merely CONTAINS 'WIP-curve' (a '## Deviations — WIP-curve notes' section would open it); falling back to whole-document scanning when no section exists (the false pass C-1 names returns for a report with no section at all); ending the section only at a heading of the same or higher level (a '### ...' subsection would then silently extend it); changes to WIP caps, graduation analysis or the other report checks (spec out of scope).
intent.why: The template already names the section, and both the template and the one real report open it with an ATX heading whose text begins 'WIP-curve'. Opening on a heading that BEGINS by naming the WIP curve (whitespace and case tolerant), closing on the next heading of any kind, and skipping fenced code with the CommonMark closing rule accepts every heading the repository actually uses and nothing that merely mentions the curve. Scoping happens in the line source of _wip_rows, so the completeness checks downstream are untouched.

Any other unit that grows attention-budget.md or clean-sweep's mandatory docs moves these callouts again; the integrator's gen-badges re-run on the union covers it (U389 note).

Setext headings (a paragraph line underlined with === or ---) END the section (round 2) but never OPEN it: the spec and the prose name ATX, and TEMPLATE.md and every report under docs/runs/ use ATX. Correction (round 3): the round-2 entry here said a list item or block quote line followed by --- 'fails closed: rows after it are refused, never bound'. That was wrong. The round-2 checker refused a complete section ('— none found'), and it also bound []: an incomplete, duplicate wave=2 row after '- a note' / '---' was never read (PR #401 P1 4012744258, reproduced by the verdict). Now (ac9395d), only a plain paragraph line or its continuation arms the setext rule. A list item or block quote line and its lazy continuation never end the section, and the fail-open repro is refused naming wave 2. The rule is still line-level, not a CommonMark parse, and two shapes remain. First, a list item's indented paragraph after a blank line ('- a', '', '  b', '---') is read as plain, so its --- ends the section. That fails closed: rows after it are refused, and none bind. Second, an ordered item not numbered 1 directly under a paragraph line ('Text', '2. a', '---') is read as a container, though CommonMark makes it paragraph text under a setext heading. The section then stays open under that heading. Neither shape is in the batch.

Indented (four-space) code blocks are not treated as code: a pipe line there still reads if it sits inside the section. This is unchanged from base, and a WIP row is a table line, which an indented block is not.

Every WIP-curve section in a report is read; a report with two sections gets one row per wave across both, so a wave duplicated between them trips the doubled-wave check (one row per wave, by design).
